author: ojiudezue
title: v5.101.4 shipped: Household routine sensor recency bound (v5.101.3 fix-up)
summary: Household routine sensor recency bound (v5.101.3 fix-up)
why: Shipped as its own release rather than folded into a later batch because it completes a property the operator explicitly asked for — 'we need to not have this be a problem if unacknowledged' — and half-delivered, that property is worse than undelivered: the person sensors self-clear while the household sensor stays pinned, which reads as an inconsistent system rather than a known gap. The miss itself is the lesson: I bounded the query I had traced and never asked how many consumers read the same rows, which is the count-the-consumers rule I have applied to other people's code all night. It was caught only because live validation was run against the real sensors instead of trusting a green suite.
implications: Shipped ROUTINE-DETECTOR-NO-DISCHARGE-1 at v5.101.4; card(s) sit shipped_organic pending validation. Acceptance in README_v5.101.4.md (Live criteria).
revisit_trigger: live: sensor.ura_coordinator_manager_household_routine_status reads something other than 'major_shift' with no button press, because its driving rows (2026-05-15..05-28) fall outside the 56-day recency window; AND the person routine sensors are unchanged from v5.101.3

refs.release_notes:
- v5.101.3 bounded the routine-status query by recency so an unacknowledged shift stops driving the sensor once it ages past the detector's 56-day baseline — making acknowledgement OPTIONAL. It bounded only ONE of TWO sensors.
- CAUGHT BY LIVE VALIDATION, NOT TESTS: after the v5.101.3 restart the Jaya sensor correctly dropped major_shift -> shifted (its May severity-4 rows aged out exactly as designed) while the HOUSEHOLD sensor still read major_shift on the same 462 rows. Two sensors, two separate queries; the person one working perfectly is what made the household one look like a broken bound rather than an untouched consumer.
- The household query now carries the same ROUTINE_STATUS_RECENCY_DAYS bound, unbounded variant preserved behind the 0 kill switch.
- The guard test was HOLLOW TWICE on this feature and both failures are documented in the README: a bare substring check (sensor.py has three queries containing it) and a SELECT-keyword span that ran 5887 chars and swallowed an unrelated predicate. Now anchored on triple-quote boundaries, asserting BOTH queries are bounded, and drilled to RED.
